lessons.title: At the train station
lessons.goal: Buy a ticket and ask about trains, platforms and connections.

tip.title: Aller simple, aller-retour
tip.body: A one-way ticket is un aller simple, a return is un aller-retour. Use pour with the destination: un billet pour Lyon. Timetables use the 24-hour clock: le train de dix-sept heures dix. Departure boards show the voie (track); people also say le quai (platform). Pronunciation: aller sounds like 'a-lay' (silent r), billet like 'bee-yay', and quai like English 'kay'.

lessons.title: Hotel requests & problems
lessons.goal: Ask for things at a hotel and explain a problem with your room.

tip.title: Polite requests: Je pourrais … ? Vous pourriez … ?
tip.body: Je pourrais avoir … ? (Could I have …?) and Vous pourriez … ? (Could you …?) are softer than je veux, which sounds rude in a hotel. To report a problem, use ne … pas: La clim ne marche pas. Pronunciation: in chambre and serviette the e is silent at the end, and in France wifi is often said 'wee-fee'.

lessons.title: At the airport
lessons.goal: Check in, find your gate and ask for help at the airport.

tip.title: Asking for help politely
tip.body: Start with Excusez-moi or Pardon, madame / monsieur — then ask. Vous pouvez m'aider ? is fine; Vous pourriez m'aider ? is even more polite. Key airport words: l'enregistrement (check-in), la porte (gate), l'embarquement (boarding), un vol (a flight), un bagage à main (hand luggage). Aéroport has four syllables: a-é-ro-port, with a silent t.

lessons.title: Je vais partir en Suisse
lessons.goal: Talk about travel plans with the futur proche and the right preposition for places.

tip.title: Futur proche + à / en / au / aux
tip.body: For plans, use aller + infinitive: je vais partir, on va prendre le TGV. Places: à + city (à Genève, à Bruxelles); en + feminine countries — most ending in -e — and countries starting with a vowel (en France, en Belgique, en Iran); au + masculine countries (au Canada, au Sénégal, au Mexique); aux + plural (aux États-Unis). Note au Québec (the province) but à Québec (the city). Make the liaison in aux‿États-Unis and en‿Italie.

story.title: Paris to Marseille
story.intro: Léa and Karim are waiting at the Gare de Lyon in Paris for their TGV to Marseille.

lines.t: Karim, regarde le panneau ! Notre TGV pour Marseille a quarante minutes de retard.

lines.name: Karim
lines.t: Ce n'est pas vrai ! On va rater le dîner chez ta sœur.

lines.t: Mesdames et messieurs, le TGV à destination de Marseille Saint-Charles partira de la voie onze, avec un retard d'environ quarante minutes.

culture.title: TGV, CFF, SNCB and VIA Rail
culture.body: France's high-speed TGV, run by SNCF, links Paris with cities like Lyon, Marseille and Bordeaux; booking early is usually much cheaper, and Ouigo is its low-cost brand. Paper tickets used to need stamping (composter) in a yellow machine before boarding — with e-tickets this is rarely needed now. In Switzerland the trains of the CFF (SBB in German) are known for punctuality, and in Belgium the network is run by the SNCB. In Canada distances are huge: VIA Rail links Québec City and Montréal, but many people drive or fly.
